notes: Main cases work, including no-site, internal-only, HTTP-only and site-wins, but two choices depart from the spec. It skips names covered by a wildcard site policy, which differs from site-block behavior. It also adds an ad-hoc heuristic that forces default issuers when http_port, https_port, cert_lifetime or default_bind are set, so output diverges from the dummy-site equivalent.

Similar to C2 (always-created policies, wildcard coverage heuristic), plus a hacky special case that injects default ACME issuers when http_port, cert_lifetime or similar options are set, which breaks the 'same as a dummy site block' requirement; tests are reasonable.

Splits names into public and internal policies and handles internal-only names, but it skips any name matched by a site wildcard. The 'custom catch-all' check compares against a policy that already contains global options, so any hostless HTTPS site plus e.g. key_type suppresses all policies, including the internal issuer for localhost; the Tailscale skip is also missing.

Handles internal-only and mixed names and keeps names listed, but always emits a policy even when it carries nothing, duplicates the site split logic, and adds wildcard and hostless-catch-all heuristics the spec did not ask for (hostless plus internal names can end up on an ACME catch-all).

Adds the names to forcedAutomatedNames and creates one global-option policy per name; it reuses an exact-subject site policy when one exists and gives non-public names an explicit internal issuer. Output consolidates to match the dummy-site case, and the tests are thorough, including a check that the HTTP app is unchanged; drawbacks are leftover empty policies when no globals are set and global options carried onto internal policies.

Compact: reuses the forcedAutomatedNames path, matches site policies by exact subject and gives internal names the internal issuer; it still differs from the reference by always creating policies (noise in the adapt output) and by writing an internal issuer into issuer-less site policies, but its tests are thorough, including error cases and an HTTP-app-unchanged check.

Copies the site-block public/internal split but omits the internal-only branch. A list of only localhost or IP names gets no internal issuer, so the empty policy is dropped and, with no HTTP auto-HTTPS, those names fall to the ACME defaults, violating an explicit requirement; the tests only cover the mixed case.

Parsing, automate-loader listing and site-policy precedence work, but a list of only internal names (e.g. just `localhost`) gets no internal issuer; that empty policy is then dropped by consolidation, so with no HTTP app the name falls back to ACME, and it always adds an empty public policy that the reference avoids.
